To draw the projections of points, we use standard reference lines ($XY$). Projector distance is given as $40\text{ mm}$.

- **(a) Point A ($30\text{ mm}$ above HP, $50\text{ mm}$ in front of VP):**
  - Front View ($a'$): $30\text{ mm}$ above $XY$.
  - Top View ($a$): $50\text{ mm}$ below $XY$.

- **(b) Point B (in HP, $40\text{ mm}$ in front of VP):**
  - Front View ($b'$): on $XY$ line.
  - Top View ($b$): $40\text{ mm}$ below $XY$.

- **(c) Point C ($50\text{ mm}$ below HP, in VP):**
  - Front View ($c'$): $50\text{ mm}$ below $XY$.
  - Top View ($c$): on $XY$ line.

- **(d) Point D ($20\text{ mm}$ above HP, $50\text{ mm}$ behind VP):**
  - Front View ($d'$): $20\text{ mm}$ above $XY$.
  - Top View ($d$): $50\text{ mm}$ above $XY$.

- **(e) Point E ($30\text{ mm}$ below HP, $40\text{ mm}$ behind VP):**
  - Front View ($e'$): $30\text{ mm}$ below $XY$.
  - Top View ($e$): $40\text{ mm}$ above $XY$.

*(Note: Draw a common reference line $XY$, erect perpendicular projector lines spaced $40\text{ mm}$ apart for each point, and mark the respective distances).*
proTip: Always remember: Front view represents distances above/below HP, and Top view represents distances in-front-of/behind VP.
